Command: Do not eat any mixture containing leaven during Passover
Summary: Nothing containing leaven — no leavened mixture of any kind — may be eaten during the Passover feast.
Commandment: Eat nothing containing leaven during the seven days of Unleavened Bread.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The rule closed every loophole: leaven was excluded not only as bread but in any mixture. Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: Scripture's stated context: the meal is eaten in haste on the night of deliverance from Egypt, ready to depart (Exodus 12:11).
